links.outcome: Legitimacy of research citations in Gemini responses, checked via PubMed and Google Scholar
links.effect: Gemini cited 16 papers in 6 of 24 responses; 12 of 16 had errors (7 unidentifiable, 5 with discrepancies in year, journal, or authorship). ChatGPT cited none.
links.quote: 12 of the 16 studies referenced contained errors and either were unable to be identified (7) or contained discrepancies (5) regarding publication year, journal, or proper accreditation of authorship.

links.outcome: Agreement of LLM responses with AAOS pediatric orthopaedic clinical practice guidelines
links.effect: ChatGPT and Gemini agreed with AAOS CPGs at 67% and 69%; no significant difference between models; neutral statements or disagreement rate was substantial.
links.quote: ChatGPT and Gemini performed similarly, agreeing with the AAOS CPGs at a rate of 67% and 69%.

screen.reason: Evaluates the accuracy and citation validity of ChatGPT and Gemini responses to pediatric orthopaedic questions derived from clinical practice guidelines, without testing a specific deployment practice or safeguard.
